section.content: 本公开的实施例涉及人工智能（AI）/机器学习（ML）模型更新。在一方面，网络设备接收AI/ML模型和第一数据集。第一数据集包括与第一标签集相关联的第一数据样本集。网络设备基于多个未标记数据样本、AI/ML模型以及在第一标签集中指示视距（LOS）路径的标签的数量与指示非视距（NLOS）路径的标签的数量的比率，获取第二数据集。网络设备基于第二数据集更新AI/ML模型的至少一个模型参数。如本公开中所提供的，可以由更新的AI/ML模型提供更高的LOS/NLOS分类精度。

Embodiments of the present disclosure relate to Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) model updates. In an aspect, a network device receives an AI/ML model and a first data set. The first data set includes a first data sample set associated with a first tag set. The network device obtains a second data set based on a plurality of unlabeled data samples, an AI/ML model, and a ratio of a number of labels in the first label set indicating line of sight (LOS) paths to a number of labels indicating non-line of sight (NLOS) paths. The network device updates at least one model parameter of the AI/ML model based on the second data set. As provided in the present disclosure, higher LOS/NLOS classification accuracy may be provided by the updated AI/ML model.

Artificial intelligence/machine learning model updateTechnical Field

Various example embodiments relate generally to the field of communications and, more particularly, relate to network devices, terminal devices, methods, apparatuses, and computer-readable storage media related to Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) model updating.

Background

In communication technology, the range of AI/ML-enabled positioning may be based on Radio Frequency (RF) fingerprinting (e.g., channel Impulse Response (CIR), etc.), as discussed in the third generation partnership project (3 GPP). In practice, some of the marker data may be collected by a Positioning Reference Unit (PRU) deployed in the network. However, it is difficult to collect enough marker data to enable large-scale model training for use cases with AI/ML-based positioning accuracy enhancement. This has prompted the study of AI/ML techniques with low tag data dependence.

Fortunately, unlabeled data containing only CIR is relatively easy to obtain. For example, one way to collect unlabeled data at the network side is for the User Equipment (UE) to report the CIR estimated from Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) measurements. In this way, a large amount of data without location tags will be acquired but a relatively small amount of data with location tags. These data can be used to train a high-precision AI/ML model.

Disclosure of Invention

In general, example embodiments of the present disclosure provide network devices, terminal devices, methods, apparatuses, and computer-readable storage media for AI/ML updating. For example, the solution provided by example embodiments of the present disclosure may allow a network device to support updating AI location models deployed at terminal devices with pseudo tags, thereby providing higher line of sight (LOS)/non line of sight (NLOS) classification accuracy.

In a first aspect, a network device is provided. The network device may include at least one processor and at least one memory storing instructions that, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the network device to at least receive an AI/ML model and a first data set from the terminal device, wherein the AI/ML model has the capability to provide an inference result of LOS/NLOS classification with a confidence level, and the first data set includes a first data sample set associated with the first label set, the first label set being a real label indicative of a LOS path or an NLOS path, obtain a second data set based on the plurality of unlabeled data samples, the AI/ML model, and a ratio of a number of labels in the first label set indicative of the LOS path to a number of labels indicative of the NLOS path, wherein the second data set includes a second data sample set associated with the second label set, the second label set being a pseudo label indicative of the LOS path or the NLOS path, and update at least one model parameter of the AI/ML model based on the second data set.

As described above, the scope of Machine Learning (ML) enabled positioning may be based on RF fingerprinting (e.g., CIR, etc.), which is one of three research projects (SIDs) in release 18 of 3GPP, as shown in table 1.

Semi-supervised learning (SSL) can also be an effective way to address this challenging task. SSL has become an emerging topic of research in the 3gpp ran1#110 conference because it is capable of providing pseudo tags for large-scale unlabeled data, an AI localization task for which there is a small amount of tagged data (e.g., { CIR/PDP, location tag }) and enough available unlabeled data { CIR/PDP; N/a location }, which is a promising solution. This is shown in table 2.

AI/ML positioning is data driven. The training of the AI/ML model is highly dependent on a large amount of marker data. However, in the real world, collecting large amounts of marked data would be difficult and costly, while unmarked data containing only CIRs is relatively easy to obtain. Thus, training SSL of a model using a combination of small amounts of tagged data and large amounts of untagged data is a reasonable solution to this challenge.

In semi-supervised learning, one approach is to first train a model based on a small labeled dataset and then use the model to generate pseudo tags on unlabeled data. By combining the original marked data with unmarked data with high confidence, the model can be fine tuned/retrained. These processes may be performed iteratively to find the best model.

However, using only unlabeled data with high confidence may not lead to a deterministic inference improvement, which may in some cases even lead to worse inference results, due to neglecting the data distribution of UE locations, e.g. the ratio between LOS and NLOS. When the selected unlabeled dataset is different from the actual UE distribution, the model will be trained to over fit over the selected unlabeled dataset, which will result in performance degradation over the actual dataset at the UE location.

Therefore, there is a need to propose a solution for training the AI/ML model with respect to LOS/NLOS ratio taking into account the actual deployment environment of the terminal device. Example embodiments of the present disclosure provide a solution for SSL for AI updating. It may allow a network device, such as an LMF/Over The Top (OTT) device, to support updating of the AI location model of the UE with artificial tagging data. The proposed solution comprises two ideas. The first idea is that the AI/ML assisted localization model provides estimated confidence as a secondary output in addition to the primary output of its LOS/NLOS classification index. The second idea is that the LMF/OTT can adjust the LOS/NLOS ratio of CIR/PDP data in the selected unlabeled dataset according to the actual deployment environment and reselect the dataset with pseudo tags for SSL training, not just based on the estimated confidence on the unlabeled data. It thus relates to new functions in UE/LMF/OTT and message exchange between entities.

The proposed solution defines the framework of SSL training methods for AI/ML model updating. The framework includes one of the methods of AI-assisted positioning. The AI model on the UE side may provide estimated confidence as a secondary output in addition to its primary LOS/NLOS classification output. The LMF may assist the UE in selecting appropriate unlabeled data from OTT based on the estimated confidence of the AI model. The framework also includes, above the LOS/NLOS estimation confidence of the AI model, the LMF can adjust the LOS/NLOS ratio of the CIR/PDP data according to the actual deployment environment and reselect the dataset with the pseudo tags (also referred to as artificial tags) for SSL training.

It should be understood that the above process steps may work together, work together in part, or be independent of each other in the operational flow described in the following sections. By implementing the embodiments of the present disclosure, updating the AI/ML model of the UE with the pseudo tag may be supported by the network device, which may provide higher LOS/NLOS classification accuracy.

Referring to fig. 1, an example network environment 100 in which example embodiments of the present disclosure may be implemented is shown. Network environment 100, which may be part of a communication network, includes a terminal device 102 and a network device 104.

As shown in fig. 1, the terminal device 102 may also be referred to as a user equipment 102 or UE 102. Network device 104 may also be referred to as LMF 104. Network device 104 may also include OTT. Alternatively, the LMF together with OTT may be referred to as a network device 104. The network device 104 may also be referred to as a network node 104. The terminal device 102 and the network device 104 may communicate with each other. In some example embodiments, the network device 104 may also be referred to as an access network device that includes at least one of an LMF or OTT device. In some example embodiments, the network device 104 may also be referred to as a core network device that includes at least one of an LMF or OTT device.

Referring to fig. 2, an example signaling process 200 of AI/ML model update is shown, according to some example embodiments of the present disclosure. Fig. 2 will be described with reference to fig. 1.

As shown in fig. 2, the network device 104 sends (204) a query message 206, the query message 206 being used to query whether the AI/ML model 224 at the terminal device 102 has the ability to provide inference results for LOS/NLOS classification with confidence level. The terminal device 102 receives 202 a query message 206 from the network device 104.

The terminal device 102 determines 208 that the AI/ML model 224 has this capability. The terminal device 102 sends (210) the AI/ML model 224 to the network device 104 along with a data set (also referred to as a first data set hereinafter). The first data set includes a set of data samples associated with a set of tags, the set of tags being real tags indicating either an LOS path or an NLOS path. The network device 104 receives (212) the AI/ML model 224 and the first data set.

Network device 104 obtains (214) a second data set based on the plurality of unlabeled data samples, AI/ML model 224, and a ratio of a number of labels in the first label set indicating LOS paths to a number of labels indicating NLOS paths. The second data set includes a second data sample set associated with a second tag set, the second tag set being a pseudo tag indicating an LOS path or an NLOS path.

The network device 104 updates (216) at least one model parameter of the AI/ML model 224 based on the second data set. The network device 104 sends 220 at least one model parameter of the updated AI/ML model 224 to the terminal device 102. The terminal device 102 receives (218) at least one model parameter of the updated AI/ML model 224.

Details of the acquisition (214) and update (216) processes will be described with reference to fig. 3-5, and therefore, for purposes of simplicity, they will not be described herein.

By implementing the embodiment of fig. 2, updating the AI/ML model of the UE with the pseudo tag may be supported by the network device. The LMF may adjust the LOS/NLOS data ratio according to the actual deployment environment and reselect the dataset with pseudo tags for SSL training, which may provide higher LOS/NLOS classification accuracy.

As shown in FIG. 3, architecture 300 includes CIP/PDP dataset 302, SSL AI/ML model 304, and LOS-NLOS reasoning results 306. The input to SSL AI/ML model 304 is the CIR/PDP vector collected from each TRP, the dimensions of which are. The output of the SSL AI/ML model 304 is the LOS/NLOS confidence 306, rather than a hard value of the LOS/NLOS classification. Referring to fig. 4, an example function 400 of a UE and LMF is shown in accordance with some example embodiments of the present disclosure. As shown in fig. 4, block 402 illustrates the UE-side functionality. The pre-trained AI/ML assisted positioning model 304 is located on the UE side and the UE also stores small-scale data 404 with real tags for model lifecycle management (LCM). On the UE side, storage and computing power is limited.

As another example, block 406 illustrates functionality of the LMF side. The LMF collects unlabeled data from UEs and maintains a large-scale unlabeled data set 408 to obtain an overview of the wireless environment. Since it is difficult to obtain enough real tags and considering the limited memory space and computational power on the UE side, we can make model updates with large scale unlabeled datasets on the LMF side and enough memory and computational power. By using SSL-based model training, the LMF can update models with higher LOS/NLOS classification accuracy.

Referring to fig. 5, another example signaling process 500 of AI/ML model update is shown, according to some example embodiments of the disclosure. Fig. 5 shows a scenario where the UE-side AI/ML model has been pre-trained with a marked dataset in a supervised manner, and the LMF 504 maintains an unmarked CIR/PDP dataset. The UE 502 in fig. 5 may correspond to the terminal device 102 in fig. 1. Together, LMF 504 and OTT 506 may correspond to network device 104 in fig. 1.

As an example, the UE 502 may be pre-trained with the marker dataset in a supervised manner (508). The LMF 504 may be ready to monitor and manage 510 the AI/ML model. OTT 506 may maintain 512 a data set with unlabeled CIR/PDP samples.

Additionally or alternatively, the UE 502 may send 514 a message 518 to the LMF 504 requesting updating of the model with SSL methods. The LMF 504 may receive 516 a message 518 from the UE 502. Alternatively, the LMF 504 may trigger (520) an update of the AI/ML model with SSL methods.

The LMF 504 may send 524 a query 526, the query 526 being used to query the AI/ML model of the UE 502 with the ability to provide AI/ML assisted location inference results (such as LOS/NLOS classification) with confidence. The UE 502 may receive 522 a query 526 from the LMF 504.

If the AI/ML model of the UE 502 is capable of providing AI/ML assisted positioning reasoning results with confidence, the UE 502 can send 528 an Acknowledgement (ACK) (532) to the LMF 504 with its AI/ML assisted positioning model and a small-scale marker dataset (e.g., CIR/PDP+tag). The LMF 504 may receive 530 an ACK (532), an AI/ML model, and a small-scale markup data set from the UE 502.

If the AI/ML model of the UE 502 is unable to provide AI/ML assisted positioning inference results with confidence, the UE 502 can send 534 a Negative Acknowledgement (NACK) to the LMF 504 (538). The LMF 504 may receive 536 a NACK 538 from the UE 502. The UE 502 may terminate the process of updating the AI/ML model with SSL methods.

The LMF 504 may select 542 unlabeled CIR/PDP data from a database in OTT with reference to unlabeled data selection criteria, e.g., inference confidence for category LOS and category NLOS, respectively.

Additionally or alternatively, the LMF 504 may calculate the inference confidence and pseudo tag the unlabeled CIR/PDP samples. For example, LOS/NLOS confidence for an unlabeled dataset can be obtained by feeding the unlabeled data into a pre-trained AI/ML auxiliary model with LOS/NLOS classification capabilities. As discussed in fig. 3, the output of the model may be a vector containing two values, the first value may be the confidence of the LOS and the second value may be the confidence of the NLOS. For example, if the output is (a=98%, b=2%), this means that the path is likely to be an LOS path. A pseudo tag may then be added to the unlabeled data for output LOS/NLOS confidence.

LMF 504 may sort the unlabeled data selected at 542 for category LOS and category NLOS, respectively (544). The LMF 504 may select the top sample from each class. LMF 504 may construct a new dataset from a combination of data from both categories with the original CIR/PDP and artificial LOS/NLOS tags.

In some example embodiments, the LOS/NLOS ratio in the marker dataset may indicate the wireless environment of the UE location (e.g., the location of UE 502). Maintaining the same LOS/NLOS ratio in the selected unlabeled dataset may help preserve the characteristics of the wireless environment of UE 502. Otherwise, there will be a drift between the two environments represented by the two data sets and LOS/NLOS accuracy will drop due to this drift.
